title: Classical spin liquids in the kagome Ising model, and their link with magnetoelasticity
authors: T. Vignau Costa, J. Colbois, G. L. Rossini, F. Mila, D. C. Cabra, S. A. Grigera, R. A. Borzi
abstract: We investigate a nearest-neighbor Ising model on the kagome lattice coupled to elastic lattice distortions. By integrating out the lattice degrees of freedom, we derive an approximate spin-only description in terms of a kagome \(J_1\)-\(J_2\)-\(J_{3}\) Ising model with interactions extending to third nearest-neighbors. Using tensor network methods complemented by classical Monte Carlo simulations, we revisit its zero-temperature phase diagram and characterize the ground states studied more than thirty years ago. We discover three phases with extensive zero-temperature entropy and algebraically decaying spin correlations. Importantly, these states are not confined to fine-tuned points or frontiers between phases, but occupy extended areas of parameter space. Their quasi long-range order is reflected in Bragg-like peaks in the structure factors; we relate this, and other properties, to diverse phases found in Ising and Heisenberg models. Finally, we trace the trajectories generated by the magnetoelastic coupling through the effective-model phase diagram, explaining the emergence of self-frustration for the unfrustrated magnetoelastic model with ferromagnetic interactions.
summary: This work analyzes classical spin liquids on the kagome lattice by coupling the Ising spins to lattice elasticity, deriving an effective $J_1-J_2-J_3$ model. Using tensor networks and Monte Carlo simulations, the authors map out the zero-temperature phase diagram, revealing multiple degenerate phases with quasi-long-range order. The findings provide a detailed understanding of how lattice coupling stabilizes exotic magnetic ground states.
main_problem: The paper investigates the nature of classical spin liquids in the kagome Ising model and how their ground states are influenced by magnetoelastic coupling to lattice distortions.
main_result: They discovered three macroscopically degenerate phases with extensive zero-temperature entropy and algebraically decaying spin correlations, which occupy extended regions of the parameter space.
method: The study employs a combination of tensor network methods (like CTMRG) and classical Monte Carlo simulations to analyze the effective spin-only Hamiltonian derived from the full magnetoelastic model.
model_or_system: The system is a nearest-neighbor Ising model on the kagome lattice coupled to elastic lattice distortions. This is mapped onto an effective $J_1-J_2-J_3$ Ising model Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Zero-temperature phase diagram, residual entropy, spin-spin correlations (algebraically decaying), and structure factors exhibiting Bragg-like peaks.
important_parameters: The coupling constants $J_1, J_2, J_3$, and the magnetoelastic coupling strength ($\alpha$ or related parameters).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on approximating the coupling by integrating out lattice degrees of freedom using a linear expansion in small ionic displacements ($\delta r$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the lattice geometry and neighbor types. Figure 3 shows the zero-temperature phase diagrams for different coupling regimes, mapping out phase boundaries.
paper_structure: The paper first derives an effective spin-only Hamiltonian by integrating out lattice fluctuations. It then uses tensor network and Monte Carlo methods to characterize the zero-temperature phase diagram of the resulting $J_1-J_2-J_3$ model, tracing the effects of magnetoelastic coupling.
why_interesting: While focused on classical magnetism, the use of advanced numerical techniques like tensor networks to solve frustrated 2D classical models is highly relevant to quantum many-body physics simulations.

A distortion at site i is indicated together with its effect on the neighboring exchange couplings and nearest-neighbors dis- tances. Circles represent Ising spins with positive (blue) and negative (red) orientation along the magnetic axis. The arrow indicates an ion displacement from the pristine lattice (bold dots) to its new position on the lattice (translucent dot). We represent with a dotted line the distances of first (light blue), second (yellow), and third (green, magenta) neighbors. We distinguish the two different third neighbors as being bridged by an intermediate site (green) or not (magenta). The unit cell is painted in gray.

Each kagome star maps to a tensor in the tensor network construc- tion shown on the right, see Eq. (11). The contraction of neighboring tensors automatically enforces the matching con- ditions for overlapping stars, as highlighted by the blue and orange rectangles.
